industry: Home Remodeling (kitchen, bath, basement, whole-home, interior)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Government look-alike design, 'official notice', fake checks or invoices (39 USC 3001)
Unsubstantiated 'best', '#1', 'voted #1', 'guaranteed results', percent-savings claims (FTC Act s.5)
Invented or composite testimonials, star ratings or review counts (16 CFR 255)
'Free' unless it truly costs nothing and carries no hidden obligation (16 CFR 251)
Fake expiration dates or fake scarcity; any deadline printed must be real
Demographic/age targeting language (e.g., 'seniors', 'retirees') unless the client has evidence it fits their actual buyers
Any vendor case-study result (calls, ROI, revenue) printed as if it were the client's own result
'Lead-safe', 'EPA certified' or the Lead-Safe Certified Firm logo unless the firm is actually RRP-certified
'Licensed', 'bonded', 'insured' unless true for the scope advertised
'Increase your home value by X%' or ROI claims unless citing the exact source and year; most remodels do not recoup cost
'Free cabinets/sink with remodel' when the remodel is bid-priced (16 CFR 251)
'0% financing' without stating it as an APR; payment or term figures without full Reg Z disclosures
compliance_notes: If the sale closes in the home: FTC Cooling-Off Rule (16 CFR 429) applies to $25+ in-home sales; the client's contract must carry the 3-day cancel notice. States can add longer windows.

Print the client's contractor license number where the state requires it in ads; requirements vary by state, and the client must confirm their own state's rule (we only verified the specific state rules named below).
Any discount or 'save X%' must be off a real, recently charged price; 'save 40%' with no reference price is not allowed.

Reg Z, 12 CFR 1026.24 (verified): if a card states a down payment amount or %, the number of payments or repayment period (e.g., 'for 24 months', 'no payments for 12 months'), a payment amount ('$99/mo'), or a finance charge amount, it must also state the down payment, the full repayment terms and the 'annual percentage rate' using that term. Any rate (e.g., '0%') must be stated as an APR. Terms must be ones actually offered. Safe alternative: 'Financing available', which uses no trigger terms. Have the lender review.

FTC 'Free' Guide, 16 CFR 251 (verified): (1) 'free with purchase' means the paid item is at its regular price (sold openly for about 30 days), with no markup or downgrade to cover the free item; (2) all conditions go right next to the offer, not in an asterisk footnote; (3) if the main job is priced by negotiation or bid, 'free [item] with purchase' is improper; (4) don't run the same 'free' offer more than 6 months in any 12; (5) 'gift' or 'bonus' wording doesn't cure a deceptive 'free'.

Warranty ads, 16 CFR 239 + 702 (verified): 'lifetime/life' must say whose or what life (239.4); 'satisfaction/money-back guarantee' only if the full price is refunded on request, with conditions disclosed (239.3); advertise a warranty only if it is promptly honored (239.5); ads should say where the full warranty can be seen (239.2).
Testimonials and star ratings must be real, typical and current; disclose any material connection (16 CFR 255).
California B&P 7030.5 (verified): license number must appear in all advertising, including postcards; ads must stay within the license classification.

EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745, verified): firms paid to disturb paint in pre-1978 homes must be certified; only certified firms may claim certification or use the Lead-Safe logo. If the client is not certified, don't imply lead-safe practice.
Home-improvement contractor registration/ad rules exist in many states (e.g., HIC registration numbers); not verified state by state here. Client must confirm.
Resale-value and 'joy' figures: cite source and year if printed (e.g., 'NAR 2025 Remodeling Impact Report'); never generalize them into a promise.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, disgust, joy, pride, status, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer.why: The #1 blocker is finding the right pro (33%). A no-obligation visit lowers risk; a free design session gives something first (reciprocity, #2). GOLD-remodeling-008/009/010 lead with a free evaluation/consultation/quote.
headline_offer_patterns: 'Free basement evaluation: see what your space could be'
Pair with a written, itemized quote promise
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Designer and homeowner at a kitchen table with sketches/samples; or the finished room the consult leads to.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: 'Free' that turns into a high-pressure sales sit-down; vague 'free estimate' buried in a service list.

combos.offer: Free in-home design consultation, no obligation
combos.photo_scene: Designer laying out cabinet samples on a homeowner's table
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: See your new kitchen before you spend a dime.

combos.headline: Turn the room you forgot into the room you need.
combos.photo_scene: Finished basement lounge from a real job
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Space for movie nights, guests and quiet.

combos.headline: A written price before any work starts.
combos.offer: Free on-site estimate with itemized quote
combos.photo_scene: PM walking a homeowner through a printed quote
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: No surprises, start to finish.

combos.headline: What would your bathroom look like done right?
combos.offer: Free design visit + 3D layout (only if offered)
combos.photo_scene: Tablet showing a 3D bath render next to the old bath
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Walk into a bathroom you love every morning.

compliance_flags: 16 CFR 251: 'free' only if truly free; state any condition next to the offer.
If the visit ends in an in-home sale of $25+, the Cooling-Off notice is required.

emotion_by_offer.why: 'Finally have the financial means' is the #2 trigger (35%); funding was a challenge for 13%. Financing turns the dream into a doable decision. Per roofing round 5 and the 2026-10-27 conflict rule, financing works best as the secondary line, not the headline.
headline_offer_patterns: Lead with the finished room; 'Financing available' as the support line
Only state a rate/term with full Reg Z disclosures
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Finished kitchen with family gathered; calm, not salesy.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Financing-first headlines that make the card read like a loan ad; '0% for 24 months' with no APR/terms (Reg Z violation).

combos.headline: The kitchen you've waited for. Now's the time.
combos.photo_scene: Family cooking together in a finished kitchen
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Stop waiting; start cooking in it this season.

combos.headline: Your dream bath, on a plan that fits.
combos.photo_scene: Spa-like finished shower with natural light
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: A daily retreat without draining savings.

combos.headline: Finish the basement. Keep your savings.
combos.offer: 0% APR for [N] months, with full Reg Z terms printed beside it (only if lender-approved)
combos.photo_scene: Finished basement with kids playing
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Room to grow without the big upfront bill.

compliance_flags: Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24: '0%' must be stated as an APR; any term/payment/down-payment figure triggers full disclosures.

emotion_by_offer.why: A specific dollar figure is easy to value (#15). GOLD-remodeling-004 (King of Kitchens: '$1,499 10x10 cabinets & granite') sells a packaged price; GOLD-003 uses '20% off'. Packaged prices remove budget fear (26% cite budget).
headline_offer_patterns: '$[X] off a full kitchen or bath remodel'
Package price: '[size] kitchen package from $[X]' with what's included
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Finished room that matches the package being priced.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Percent-off with no regular price; package photos showing upgrades not included in the price.

combos.headline: $[X] off a full bathroom remodel.
combos.photo_scene: Bright finished bathroom from the client's portfolio
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: A bathroom you're proud to show guests.

combos.offer: Package price with inclusions listed on the front
combos.photo_scene: The exact package installed in a real kitchen
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: A fresh kitchen without a budget surprise.

combos.headline: Save $[X] on your basement finish.
combos.photo_scene: Finished basement game room
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Your family's favorite room, for less.

compliance_flags: Discount off a real recent price; package must match the photo.
'Free sink with countertop' only if the countertop is sold at a regular, non-negotiated price (GOLD-007 'free undermount sink' needs that check).

emotion_by_offer.why: GOLD-remodeling-005 (Clear Choice Bath): 'We Just Remodeled Your Neighbor's Bathroom!' Local descriptive norms move behavior (Goldstein et al. 2008).
headline_offer_patterns: '[N] projects in [neighborhood] this year' (only if true)
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Real finished project in that neighborhood (permission), similar architecture.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Fake proximity claims; photos from another region or a stock image.

combos.photo_scene: Finished bath from a nearby home
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Get the bathroom your neighbors are talking about.

combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Less hassle, faster start.

compliance_flags: Only real nearby jobs; get written photo/name consent.

emotion_by_offer.primary_emotion: anticipation / fear of missing a real date
emotion_by_offer.why: Real deadlines create urgency (#10). Remodel-specific seasonal hooks ('done before the holidays') are an inference from the long project timelines, not tested.
headline_offer_patterns: 'Book by [date] to be done before [holiday]' (only if the schedule really allows)
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Finished dining/kitchen set for a gathering.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Deadlines that roll over every month; 'before the holidays' promises the crew can't meet.

combos.headline: Host the holidays in a brand-new kitchen.
combos.photo_scene: Holiday table in a finished kitchen
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Gather everyone in the kitchen you're proud of.

combos.headline: Spring projects book fast. Get on the calendar.
combos.photo_scene: Sunny finished sunroom or kitchen
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Enjoy the new room all summer.

combos.headline: This month only: $[X] off your bath.
combos.photo_scene: Finished bath
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: A better start to every day, sooner.

compliance_flags: Deadline must be real; don't promise completion dates you can't keep (FTC Act s.5).

emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Boxes in a half-finished room transforming into a styled room.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Implying you know personal purchase details; condescending 'your house is ugly'.

combos.photo_scene: Before/after of a dated vs updated kitchen

emotion_by_offer.why: Budget (26%) and schedule (19%) are named challenges; a written commitment answers them. Must be real and honored.
headline_offer_patterns: Workmanship warranty with stated length and where to read terms
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: PM handing over a printed schedule/warranty.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Vague 'satisfaction guaranteed' (requires full refund under 16 CFR 239.3); 'lifetime' without whose life.

combos.offer: Written schedule + fixed quote (only if the client does this)
combos.photo_scene: PM with a homeowner reviewing a printed timeline
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Your project, on time and on budget.

combos.photo_scene: Craftsman finishing tile
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: Peace of mind long after we leave.

combos.photo_scene: Homeowner signing off on a tablet
combos.sell_the_outcome_line: You stay in control of the cost.

compliance_flags: 16 CFR 239: state warranty length, whose 'lifetime', where full terms are; honor promptly.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-home-remodeling-001 'Voted #1 Home Improvement Business in the Area' vs FTC Act s.5
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins. Only print a ranking if it names the real source and year and is substantiated.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-home-remodeling-012 '0% financing available' vs Reg Z
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins. State it as '0% APR' with terms, or use 'Financing available'.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold/vendor ROI figures (e.g., GOLD-010 '340%-516% ROI', GOLD-008 '391%') vs never print unverified numbers
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: These are vendor-published and unaudited; use them only as weak evidence that the format can work, never on a card.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold cards often lead with a service list (GOLD-006, 011) vs C-3PO HS-04/HS-05 and Patrick's sell-the-outcome rule
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Patrick's rule + C-3PO's evidence win: outcome headline and finished-room photo on the front; service list on the back.
